pattern_name: Unilateral Interest Rate Revision
pattern_description: Lender reserves sole discretion to hike interest rates, spreads, or margins at any time without requiring the borrower's prior consent.
why_risky: The bank can increase your monthly EMI or tenure at will without your permission, significantly increasing your total cost of borrowing.
mitigation_tip: Demand linking to an external transparent benchmark (such as RBI Repo Rate/EBLR) with explicit 30-day prior written notice before changes.

pattern_name: Unconditional Personal Guarantee & Asset Seizure
pattern_description: Requires business owners, promoters, or family members to pledge unlimited personal liability covering personal bank accounts, family homes, and non-business assets.
keywords: waive right to notice as guarantor
why_risky: If your business encounters hardship, the lender can directly seize your personal residence, family savings, and personal bank accounts even before liquidating business assets.
mitigation_tip: Cap the guarantee strictly to your proportional equity share or limit recovery solely to primary hypothecated commercial assets.

pattern_name: Strict Acceleration Clause (Immediate Demand on Minor Breach)
pattern_description: Allows the lender to declare the entire loan balance immediately due and payable upon a single delayed payment or technical paperwork delay without an adequate grace period.
why_risky: A single minor administrative mistake or temporary 10-day delay could force your business into insolvency as the bank demands the full principal overnight.
mitigation_tip: Insist on a mandatory 15-to-30-day cure period (grace period) following written notice before any acceleration remedy can be triggered.

pattern_name: Prohibitive Prepayment Penalty & Extended Lock-In
pattern_description: Imposes exorbitant exit fees (e.g., 3.5%–6% + GST) or a rigid multi-year lock-in prohibiting refinancing or early debt clearance.
why_risky: Traps you in an expensive high-interest loan and penalizes you when your business has surplus cash to become debt-free or refinance at better market rates.
mitigation_tip: For individual borrowers and MSE floating loans, RBI rules prohibit foreclosure penalties; ensure zero penalty for prepayments made from business cash flows.

pattern_name: Sweeping Right of Set-Off Across All Accounts
pattern_description: Allows the lender to unilaterally freeze or debit any account, fixed deposit, or affiliated company balance held anywhere within the banking institution.
why_risky: The bank can unexpectedly freeze your company payroll account or personal savings without prior warning, paralyzing business operations.
mitigation_tip: Exclude payroll, employee statutory dues, and trust accounts from any blanket set-off provision.

pattern_name: Cross-Default Trigger
pattern_description: A clause stating that any dispute, delay, or technical breach under any unrelated third-party facility automatically triggers a default under this agreement.
keywords: deemed to be in default under all facilities
why_risky: An isolated dispute over a minor vendor invoice or personal credit card can immediately trigger a catastrophic default on your primary commercial loan.
mitigation_tip: Restrict cross-default triggers to material financial defaults above a specific monetary threshold (e.g. > ₹10,00,000) and require formal default declaration.

pattern_name: Mandatory One-Sided Arbitration & Faraway Jurisdiction
pattern_description: Restricts dispute resolution to a sole arbitrator appointed solely by the lender, often in a distant jurisdiction, while stripping the borrower of local court remedies.
keywords: arbitration award final and binding without appeal
why_risky: Severely handicaps your legal defense by requiring expensive travel and proceedings before a lender-selected arbitrator.
mitigation_tip: Ensure mutual appointment of a neutral arbitrator and seat dispute resolution in your home business jurisdiction.

pattern_name: Blanket Power of Attorney (POA) & Unilateral Asset Sale
pattern_description: Borrower irrevocably appoints the lender as attorney-in-fact to sign, transfer, assign, or sell any borrower property without judicial oversight.
why_risky: Grants the lender extraordinary unchecked authority to execute binding sale or mortgage deeds on your company's valuable assets without court supervision.
mitigation_tip: Limit power of attorney strictly to ministerial document perfection rather than direct commercial disposal.

pattern_name: Compounding Penal Charges on Default
pattern_description: Levying excessive penal interest (e.g. 24% to 36% p.a.) and compounding penal interest onto principal monthly, creating an inescapable debt trap.
why_risky: Penal compounding causes overdue balances to spiral exponentially. RBI guidelines explicitly prohibit capitalization of penal charges.
mitigation_tip: Ensure penal charges are levied strictly on a simple, non-capitalized basis in compliance with RBI Fair Practice Code circulars.

pattern_name: Broad Unilateral Change of Terms / Negative Covenants
pattern_description: Bank reserves the right to amend covenants, fee schedules, or operational rules at any time merely by updating their general website or notice board.
keywords: modify terms from time to time
why_risky: You could unknowingly violate new terms that were never directly communicated or explicitly agreed upon.
mitigation_tip: Require that material amendments to terms and conditions must be formally executed in writing signed by both parties.

pattern_name: Balloon Payment / Refinancing Cliff Trap
pattern_description: Features low initial monthly installments with an immense un-amortized lump-sum balance due on the final maturity date.
why_risky: If market liquidity tightens or your revenue dips when the balloon payment comes due, you could face sudden default and foreclosure if unable to refinance.
mitigation_tip: Ensure the loan structure amortizes smoothly over the entire tenure, or secure pre-agreed refinancing options before signing.

pattern_name: Mandatory Post-Dated Cheques (PDC) Criminal Clause Exposure
pattern_description: Requires submitting numerous undated security cheques allowing the bank to trigger Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act criminal proceedings upon commercial default.
why_risky: Commercial loan defaults can be converted into criminal proceedings with threat of arrest if the lender deposits undated security cheques without authorization.
mitigation_tip: Refuse undated blank cheques; provide modern electronic e-NACH mandates where payments are handled through standard civil commercial channels.

pattern_name: Subjective Material Adverse Change (MAC) Trigger
pattern_description: Gives the lender the arbitrary power to declare a default whenever they 'deem' in their sole judgment that your financial condition or business sector has deteriorated.
keywords: in the opinion of the lender
why_risky: The bank can cancel your credit line or demand early repayment during general economic downturns even if you have never missed a single payment.
mitigation_tip: Tie Material Adverse Change strictly to objective financial breaches (e.g. audited net worth reduction > 30%) rather than subjective bank opinion.

pattern_name: 100% Mandatory Cash Sweep on Asset Sales
pattern_description: Demands that all gross proceeds from any normal business equipment upgrade, property sale, or subsidiary divestment be seized for debt prepayment.
why_risky: Prevents your business from reinvesting capital into new, modern equipment or using asset sale proceeds to manage operational restructuring.
mitigation_tip: Allow asset disposal reinvestment within a 6-to-12-month window for replacement productive equipment before any mandatory prepayment sweep applies.

pattern_name: Immediate Waiver of Statutory SARFAESI 60-Day Notice
pattern_description: Clause attempting to make the borrower waive statutory protections or notice periods mandated under Indian security enforcement laws.
why_risky: Strips your legal defense window under the SARFAESI Act, risking swift physical repossession of plant or property without proper legal review.
mitigation_tip: Statutory notice rights under the SARFAESI Act cannot be legally waived; ensure agreements explicitly reflect mandatory 60-day Section 13(2) notices.

pattern_name: Forced Insurance Bundling & Single-Vendor Monopoly
pattern_description: Mandates that borrower must purchase expensive property, life, or loan insurance exclusively through the lender's proprietary insurance partner at inflated premiums.
keywords: mandatory insurance policy as condition precedent
why_risky: Inflates the total cost of credit through uncompetitive insurance premiums and locks you into policies that may offer inferior coverage.
mitigation_tip: Under RBI guidelines, borrowers have the legal right to procure required comprehensive insurance from any IRDAI-licensed insurer of their choice.

pattern_name: Involuntary Equity Conversion / Warrant Attachment
pattern_description: Authorizes the lender upon default or covenant breach to unilaterally convert outstanding debt into equity shares at a heavy distress discount.
why_risky: You could lose majority control of your business to the lender or distress funds without adequate compensation.
mitigation_tip: Insist that any debt-to-equity conversion must be mutually approved with valuations performed by an independent SEBI-registered valuer.

pattern_name: Negative Pledge Restricting Ordinary Working Capital
pattern_description: Prohibits the borrower from obtaining normal unsecured trade credit, supplier vendor financing, or leasing equipment necessary for daily factory operations.
keywords: no further indebtedness of any kind
negative pledge on all trade credit
prior consent for all supplier terms
why_risky: Constrains day-to-day business agility by requiring cumbersome written bank consents before taking normal supplier 30-day payment terms.
mitigation_tip: Carve out permitted indebtedness for customary trade credit and operational working capital under a defined threshold.

pattern_name: Sweeping Borrower Indemnity Without Negligence Carveout
pattern_description: Requires the borrower to indemnify the bank against all losses, expenses, and damages including situations arising from the lender's own gross negligence or administrative errors.
keywords: against all claims and losses whatsoever
why_risky: You could be forced to pay the bank's legal expenses and losses even when the dispute was caused by the bank's own accounting mistake.
mitigation_tip: Add standard carveouts: 'except in cases of the Lender's proven gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.'

pattern_name: Forfeiture of Processing & Upfront Sanction Fees
pattern_description: Lender charges massive upfront fees and states they are 100% non-refundable even if the bank fails to disburse funds due to its own internal reasons.
keywords: retained by bank irrespective of disbursement
why_risky: You lose significant capital (1%–2% of facility amount) if the lender changes internal policy or delays disbursement indefinitely.
mitigation_tip: Ensure processing fees are refundable (less reasonable administrative actuals) if the lender fails to disburse the loan through no fault of the borrower.
